subject: Per-token ladder: breakpoints and marginal vs blended options (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lawson <emma@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Per-token ladder: initial framing and two simple options

Emma —

Thanks again for taking the call last week. As promised, I pulled together a compact starting proposal for Acme's hosted-API consumption that highlights two approaches we see customers ask for when they hit the 100M+ token/month band: a marginal-breakpoint ladder (marginal pricing per tier) vs a blended-tier (effective rate averaged across committed volume).

High-level ask from our side: which pricing semantics would be easier for your finance/procurement to evaluate and forecast — (A) marginal breakpoints (clear per-token price at each band) or (B) a blended effective rate tied to committed volume (simpler monthly invoice math)? Either direction is implementable; the tradeoffs are around predictability and invoice simplicity.

I attached a short PDF with the two compact options and a one-sheet math example. I also attached a spreadsheet model for the volume scenarios you mentioned on the call. Quick notes:
- We can support monthly true-ups or quarterly true-ups — you choose what works operationally.
- We can include a small burst buffer (free credits for spikes) if you want to avoid immediate rate escalation.
- Commitment term options: 6 months pilot (convertible) or 12-month committed band with SLA.

Attachments: 20290701-Acme-per-token-proposal-v1.pdf (summary), per_token_model_acme_v1.xlsx (detailed math).

Can you confirm which style (marginal vs blended) you prefer and which monthly volume baseline you'd like us to model (100M / 200M / 500M tokens)? If you'd like, we can prepare a short 20-minute call to walk through the math.

Best,
Diego Fernandez

Subject: Re: Per-token ladder: initial framing and two simple options

Diego —

Thanks for the materials. A couple of clarifying questions before I share with finance: 
1) For the marginal ladder option, how does invoicing look if we spike above the top breakpoint inside the month? Is there a cap or overage rate?
2) For blended, can you show the effective rate math for 200M tokens/month and for a 12-month committed term? We need a single "per-token" number my CFO can compare to competitors.
3) Is there a true-up cadence you recommend (monthly vs quarterly) from an ops perspective? We run predictable weekly jobs but sometimes have end-of-month burst patterns.

Also: procurement will ask about credits for failed calls/timeout retries. Do you have standard language for how retry tokens are treated?

Can you send updated examples and a recommended default we can present internally?

—Emma Lawson
Head of Platform Integrations — Acme Health
emma@acmehealth.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lawson <emma@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2029 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-token ladder: initial framing and two simple options

Emma —

Great questions. Short answers first, then the numbers.

1) Spike handling (marginal ladder): we recommend an overage rate equal to the top-tier marginal price, applied only to tokens above the top breakpoint. Optionally we can set a hard cap (monthly invoice ceiling) if you prefer a known maximum — we usually negotiate that for enterprise finance teams.

2) Blended math example (12-mo commit, 200M tokens/month):
- Commit shape: 0-50M @ $0.012/token, 50-150M @ $0.009/token, 150-500M @ $0.006/token (marginal band prices).
- If blended: effective rate = (sum of marginal spend) / total tokens.
Example compute: for 200M tokens
  - First 50M = 50M * $0.012 = $600,000
  - Next 100M = 100M * $0.009 = $900,000
  - Remaining 50M = 50M * $0.006 = $300,000
  - Total spend = $1,800,000 -> effective blended rate = $1,800,000 / 200M = $0.009/token.

3) Recommended true-up cadence: quarterly true-ups balance operational overhead and forecast accuracy for customers with bursty end-of-month activity. Monthly true-ups give closer alignment but can increase ops churn. We usually default to monthly for pilots under 3 months, quarterly for 12+ month committed contracts.

Retry/failed calls: our standard language is to exclude obvious server-side errors (HTTP 5xx) after retry detection; client retries are typically billable because they represent additional work. We can include a short SLA clause and an example token-credit calculation in the contract.

Attached I pushed an updated spreadsheet with the 200M blended example and a second tab that shows marginal monthly invoices under three spike scenarios. Link to the sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1AcmePerTokenModel

Let me know if you'd like me to convert the blended example into a single-line per-token quote for your CFO — happy to provide a short comparison table vs a pure marginal invoice.

Best,
Diego

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Jul 2029 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-token ladder: initial framing and two simple options

Diego / Monica —

Notes from an internal ops/pricing perspective before we finalize a customer-facing sheet: 
- For enterprise buys where the buyer wants "one number" for finance, offer the blended effective rate but attach a marginal waterfall appendix so legal/ops can map actual token usage to internal cost buckets. Keeps invoices simple while preserving auditability.
- Suggest adding an optional monthly invoice ceiling (cap) for the first 3 months; helps procurement sign-off on pilots. We can amortize any discounted overage under a credit program if true-ups exceed committed volume.
- For retry credits: add a deterministic rule (e.g., auto-credit any batch where >30% of calls to the route returned 5xx) rather than ad-hoc credits — reduces negotiation friction.
- If Acme wants a burst buffer, propose 10% free burst credits in month 1 of the pilot only; resets after pilot or converts to paid buffer at a discounted marginal rate.

I'll volunteer to run the model for a 6/12/24 month comparison and include effective monthly cashflow impact for procurement. If Diego wants, we can attach that as a short one-page addendum.

Rishi
Director, Deal Structuring — Redwood Inference

Emma —

Option A (Marginal ladder / clear per-tier pricing) — 12-mo committed
- Breakpoints: 0-50M @ $0.012, 50-150M @ $0.009, 150-500M @ $0.006
- Overage above 500M @ $0.006 (top tier) unless a monthly cap is negotiated
- Quarterly true-up (default)
- Pilot burst buffer: 10% free credits for month 1

Option B (Blended single-line rate) — 12-mo committed
- For your 200M baseline example, blended effective rate = $0.009/token (see math below)
- Applies to monthly invoices as a single-line item with quarterly true-up reconciliation against actual marginal usage
- We include marginal waterfall appendix for auditability

Retry/failed calls: server-side 5xx errors auto-credit after detection; client retry tokens billable. We'll provide contract language.

Next steps:
- If either option looks good, sign the pilot via this DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/acrobat/sign?doc=ACME-PER-TOKEN-TERM
